name: Five Star Business Finance Ltd
tagline: Secured small-business lender with structurally high NIMs -- but FY26 was a down year (PAT -3%, RoE to ~16%), asset quality is deteriorating (GNPA 3.4%, 30+ DPD ~13%) and senior compliance staff have left
business_overview: Five Star Business Finance is an NBFC lending small-ticket (average ~Rs 4 lakh, LTV ~40%) secured loans to informal-income small-business owners, ~95% against self-occupied residential property, concentrated in Tamil Nadu / Andhra / Telangana. Yields ~23-24%; 100% secured book; historically low leverage (~2x) with plans to lever up toward ~4x.
fundamentals_table: ~Rs 13,240 Cr, +11% YoY in FY26 (was +23% in FY25) -- growth decelerating
FY26 PAT ~Rs 269 Cr, -3% YoY; Q1 FY27 credit cost still elevated
GNPA ~3.4% (from ~2.6%), 30+ DPD ~12.7%, PCR cut to ~41% from ~45%; NIM ~16-17%
CAR >50%; guiding no equity dilution for 3-5 years; promoters exercised warrants at a premium
fundamentals_narrative: The historically attractive part -- 'MFI-like spreads with housing-finance-like security', ~24% yields on a 100% secured book, very high CAR -- is intact. But every recent trend is the wrong way: AUM growth has halved to ~11%, FY26 PAT declined, RoE fell ~260 bps, 30+ DPD is near 13%, GNPA has risen and the company simultaneously cut provision coverage. Back-to-back resignations of the heads of Compliance and Audit (Mar 2025) and a notably evasive Q1 FY27 opening commentary have added a management-quality question on top of the credit cycle.
technical_read: Not pulled -- stock is well off its highs, near the lower half of its 52-week range on the asset-quality stress.
sentiment_summary: Read the most recent 50 posts (#7-58), May 2023 to Aug 2026. The arc is clear: 2023-early 2024 was an enthusiastic growth thesis (Nomura/ICICI coverage, 35% guidance, 'MFI spreads with HFC risk'); from late 2024 the tone turned as MFI-sector stress spread and management commentary softened. rks00, a long-standing invested bull, wrote a pointedly disappointed note in Jan 2026 -- dismal quarter, 30+ DPD near 13%, PCR cut below 40%, normalised PBT/PAT down ~6%, and doubt about Five Star's edge as it moves up into the Rs 3-10 lakh segment 'where every bank and NBFC already plays'. ranvir (trusted, elevated-tier) posts neutral quarterly concall notes. himanshu.dugar (trusted, elevated-tier) contributed earlier explanatory posts on the NIM structure, not a recent call.
community_signal: No current roster high-conviction call. The most committed long-term bull on the thread (rks00, non-roster) has turned cautious/disappointed. Trusted users (ranvir, himanshu.dugar) appear only with neutral/explanatory posts.

trusted_signals.note: Explained that Five Star's ~17-24% NIM is largely a function of low leverage plus fixed 21-24% lending rates, and that spreads/NIMs should compress as leverage rises. Analytical, not a conviction call; pre-dates the FY26 deterioration.

bse_notes: Back-to-back resignations of Key Managerial Personnel heading Compliance and Audit (disclosed Mar 2025). Promoter warrant exercise at a premium to then-market (FY26). No regulatory action noted.
bull_case: Differentiated niche: 100% secured, small-ticket (~Rs 4 lakh), ~40% LTV lending to informal small businesses at ~24% yields
Very high capital adequacy (>50%), low leverage with headroom, and a stated no-dilution runway of 3-5 years
If this is the trough (management's claim), normalised earnings power and RoE could recover as credit costs mean-revert
bear_case: FY26 PAT declined, RoE fell to ~16%, AUM growth halved to ~11% -- the compounding story has stalled
Asset quality deteriorating (GNPA ~3.4%, 30+ DPD ~13%) while provision coverage was cut -- a poor combination
Heads of Compliance and Audit both resigned in 2025; recent concall communication seen as evasive on NPAs
Moving up-market into the Rs 3-10 lakh segment puts it head-to-head with banks/NBFCs where its doorstep-underwriting edge is unproven
verdict_headline: A quality niche lender in a genuine down-cycle -- decelerating growth and rising stress, not an inflection
verdict_reasoning: thesis_fit neither: a ~Rs 16,000 Cr NBFC with mid-teens and falling RoE, ~11% AUM growth and rising credit stress has no path to 10x in 2-3 years or the ~47%+ sustained CAGR a 100x/10-year outcome needs

The recent-inflection rule does not rescue this name -- the latest data points are deterioration (PAT down, RoE down, DPD up, PCR cut), not a credible near-term positive turn; management's 'this is the trough' is so far unverified
First-time deep read; no formal red-flag tier, though the Compliance/Audit-head resignations and evasive commentary are governance yellow flags; no trusted conviction call, so no floor
Conviction Low. No 30-day revisit. Re-check trigger: two consecutive quarters of falling 30+ DPD with PCR rebuilt and RoE turning back up toward the high-teens.

four_box.note: Verdict explicit: latest data points are 'deterioration (PAT down, RoE down, DPD up, PCR cut), not a credible near-term positive turn' (tailwind=no); 'no path to 10x... or the ~47%+ sustained CAGR a 100x/10-year outcome needs' (tam=no); Compliance/Audit-head resignations are governance yellow flags.
